newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - March 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - March 14.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY

- Financial services group Board of Executors (BoE) and NBS Boland have formed a strategic association throug BoE's acquisition of a 17.2 percent stake in NBS Boland for R1.4 billion and the simultaneous purchase by NBS Boland of a 24.3 percent interest in BoE for R880 million.
- Finance Minister Trevor Manuel's restrictive budget for 1997/98 would make it easier to cut interest rates later this year, Reserve Bank governor Chris Stals said.
- Malaysian property group Metroplex Berhad could play a key role in a planned R4 billion upgrading and revitalisation of 40 hectares of Johannesburg's beleaguered city centre.

- Producer inflation went up to 9.2 percent in January, compared to 8.8 percent in December -- its highest level in eighteen months -- driven by increases in imported and local components, the Central Statistical Service said.

- The first important working day of the National Council of Provinces was cut short on Thursday amid claims that President Nelson Mandela was ill, despite assurances from his office that he was "resting".
BUSINESS REPORT

- The Fedics Group, the diversified catering and hospitality industry player, is on the point of signing an estimated R130 million black empowerment deal and is expected to seek a JSE listing as part of the unbundling of parent companies Servgro and ICS, sources said.
- The Board of Executors and the newly merged NBS/Boland Bank have undertaken a number of strategic cross shareholdings in a complex series of deals totalling more that R2.2 billion.

- Liberty Life, South Africa's third largest assurer, used a combination of local growth and good international investments to lift attributable profit by 27.8 percent to R1.54 billion in fiscal 1996, the company said.

- Gold prices on international markets will not fall much further and the metal is now considered cheap for the physical market, said Kelvin Williams, the marketing director of Anglo American's gold division, Anglogold, said.

- The Communication Worker's Union threatened on Thursday to launch militant industrial action and to call a strike in a bid to cripple Telkom and the Post Office if its demands for real wage increases are not met.
SAKE BEELD
- The enlarged bank group NBS Boland Ltd has taken on an important partner and shareholder, Board of Executors, which paid the bank R1.4 billion rand for a 17,2 percent stake.
- The Liberty Life group last year, thanks to foreign investment supported by a weak rand, lifted its earnings per share by 24,8 percent to 622 cents.
- The government admitted on Thursday that it has not achieved its tasks of rationalising and restructuring the civil service.
- The Communication Worker's Union is demanding salary increases of between 17 and 21 percent.
THE STAR

- The Middle East was plunged into a crisis on Thursday when a Jordanian soldier fired his assault rifle at a group of Israeli schoolgirls sightseeing in the Jordan Valley, killing seven and wounding six.

- When important people from organisations such as the Red Cross Society visited Robben Island, the jailed leadership of the ANC, PAC and SWAPO were spared hard labour in the lime quarry and made to perform meaningless gardening tasks instead.
- Malaysian property group Metroplex Berhad is to play a big role, in partnership with black and white local companies, in a proposed R4-billion upgrading of central Johannesburg.

- Benjamin Woods looks like any three-year-old but he reads 25 books a week, can operate the sound system, the VCR, talk about current affairs and, to top it all, his favourite companion is an IBM computer notebook. In Britain the Mensa organisation is checking if he is the youngest genius in the world.
